note: The v6 question set: v5 tuned against a 59-article answer key (research/experiments/2026-09-27-answer-key): act gains only_mentions_him, fact gets boundaries, centrality and source clearer definitions, firmness four levels composed with fact. Machine answers, not labels.

centrality.instructions: How central is the watched fighter to this article? Judge by how much of the article is about him - his part of the main news the article is built on - not by whether the article carries news about him (other questions ask that) and not by what its first sentences say.

options.not_in_content: He is not in the article's content at all.
options.one_of_several: He is one of several subjects and gets real content of his own, more than a line or two.

source.instructions: Whose words or act is the new thing this article carries about the watched fighter? The person it ORIGINATED with - never the outlet, website or account that relayed it. If a journalist or podcaster passes on what someone else said, the source is that someone. If several, the one the article's main news is built on. 'His' means the WATCHED fighter's. If the article carries nothing new about him, answer for whose words or act its main content is.

options.himself: The watched fighter speaks, posts or writes, and his words are what the article is built on.
options.his_team: People who work on his fighting: his coaches, trainers, conditioning staff, sparring partners, physio, doctor.
options.his_manager: His manager, agent or business representative.
options.opponent_side: A fighter he is booked against or publicly linked to a fight with, or that fighter's coach or manager.
options.promotion: The promotion and its officials (the UFC, its president, matchmakers, official channels), athletic commissions, official records.
options.other_fighter: Any other fighter not booked or linked with him, however famous, including champions of other divisions, friends and teammates.
options.media: A journalist, pundit, podcaster or analyst in their own voice, or the outlet's own writer; also a leak or report with no named person behind it.
options.fans: Fan reaction, social media crowds, comment sections.
options.no_one: Nobody's words are the news: an event is reported as fact and nobody is quoted or credited with announcing it.
options.none_of_these: None of the options above describes this article; a different answer is needed.

act.instructions: What does the source do regarding the watched fighter? Pick the one the article's main news is built on.

options.reports_an_event: Nobody's words are the news: something happened - he fought, weighed in, faced off, was booked, a fight of his was announced or cancelled.
options.speaks_of_himself: He himself talks about his own situation, plans, past, condition, fight or life.
options.assesses_him: Someone other than him judges him: his level, chances, performance, condition, style, place in the division.
options.predicts_his_fight: Someone other than him gives a pick or forecast for a specific fight of his: who wins, how, in which round.
options.calls_him_out: Someone other than him asks to fight him, challenges him, or trash-talks him.
options.answers_for_him: A reply to an attack, a callout or a claim aimed at him - made on his behalf by someone else, or by him.
options.steers_him: Someone other than him says what he should do next: whom he should fight, whether a rematch should happen, when to return, which weight class - including demands made on his behalf.
options.gives_news_of_him: Someone other than him gives a factual update about him: his condition, recovery, training, whereabouts, mood or plans.
options.only_mentions_him: He is only named or mentioned: in a list, a card, a comparison, as background to someone else's story. Nobody says or does anything regarding him.
options.none_of_these: None of the options above describes this article; a different answer is needed.

fact.instructions: What new FACT about the fighter named in watched_fighter does the article carry, if any? A fact is something that happened or is set to happen, not an opinion about him. Choose by the article's main news. An interview, a press conference or a media day is a place where things are said, not a fact: if something said there is the news, choose that fact, or none if it is only talk. If the article's news is about another fighter, or is only opinion, answer no fact, even when his past fights are mentioned.

options.next_fight: News of his next fight: an opponent, a date, an offer, talks, a cancellation, or when he will be ready to fight again.
options.result: The outcome of a fight of his, as the article's news: a fight report, his bout on a results page, an article built on his win or loss.
options.fight_week_event: The routine of a fight of his, and nothing more: a weigh-in, a face-off, an open workout, the card order, start times, how to watch.
options.health: An injury, a medical issue, surgery or recovery.
options.career_move: Retirement, a contract, a move of weight class or team, a title vacated, stripped or awarded.
options.personal_life: His life outside the cage: family, childhood, home, hobbies, money, a life lesson.
options.no_fact: Only opinion or talk: no new fact about him.
options.none_of_these: None of the options above describes this article; a different answer is needed.

firmness.instructions: How established is the main fact this article asserts about the watched fighter? If it asserts no fact, judge the firmest claim it makes about him.

options.none: No fact about him is asserted (the fact answer is no fact): set in code, not asked.
options.wish: A wish or a demand: someone wants it or says it should happen.
options.rumour: A rumour: unnamed sources, a leak, 'talks', 'discussions', 'plans'.
options.reported: Reported: a named outlet or journalist states it, citing sources.
options.official_or_done: Official or done: the promotion or he himself states it, or it has happened.

reports_his_result.instructions: Does this article report, as its news, the outcome of a fight of the fighter named in watched_fighter?

options.yes: probability of yes above 70%. The outcome of his fight is part of what the article reports: a fight report or recap of his bout, his bout on a results page or card results, or an article built on his win or loss.
options.no: probability of yes below 30%. His past fight is only recalled as background to other news, such as a next opponent, an interview, a quarrel or a rematch talk; or the fight is someone else's and he is not in it.

reports_his_next_fight.instructions: Does this article report news of the next fight of the fighter named in watched_fighter: an opponent, a date, an offer, a cancellation, or when he will be ready?

options.yes: probability of yes above 70%. The article reports something about his next fight as happening or planned: an opponent or a date set, offered, negotiated or cancelled, or when he will be ready to fight again.
options.no: probability of yes below 30%. Nothing about his next fight, or only wishes and opinions about it (someone calling him out, a pundit saying who he should fight), or his recovery with no word on when he can fight; or the next fight of another fighter that does not involve him.

reports_his_health.instructions: Does this article report, as its news, an injury, illness, medical procedure or recovery of the fighter named in watched_fighter?

options.yes: probability of yes above 70%. His injury, illness, procedure or recovery is part of what the article reports, including an update on how he is doing.
options.no: probability of yes below 30%. A past fight's damage or injury only recalled as background to other news; only when he will be ready to fight, with no injury or recovery described; or someone else's health.

he_speaks.instructions: Does the fighter named in watched_fighter speak in this article: a quote of his, an answer of his in an interview, or a post he wrote?

options.yes: probability of yes above 70%. His own words appear in the article.
options.no: probability of yes below 30%. Only other people speak, including other fighters, his opponent, or his manager or coach speaking about him; or his name appears without any words of his.
